description: CE migration replaces users_user_type_check so users.user_type accepts 'internal' | 'client' | 'service' (DROP CONSTRAINT, ADD … NOT VALID, VALIDATE; Citus-safe)
CE migration creates service_principals(tenant, user_id, kind, name, description, allow_act_as, created_by, archived_at, created_at, updated_at) with PK (tenant, user_id)
EE migration adds agents.service_user_id; all readers of metadata.backing_user_id switch to the column

CE migration adds nullable via-principal columns: time_entries.created_via_principal_id/updated_via_principal_id, time_sheets.approved_via_principal_id, schedule_entries/interactions/comments/project_tasks.created_via_principal_id, tickets.entered_via_principal_id, ticket_audit_logs.via_principal_user_id; EE adds mcp_agent_audit.act_as_user_id
CE migration adds api_rate_limit_settings.principal_user_id with unique (tenant, principal_user_id)
CE migration adds nullable tenants.service_principal_limit (platform-admin override)
Migration adds RBAC resource service_principal (read/create/update/delete) and seeds it to the Admin role

TypeScript/Zod user-type unions widened to include 'service' where a service user can appear (IUser, shared IUser, AuthorizationSubject.userType, UserSession, event-bus schema); login/SSO/portal types stay internal|client
Stale API userTypeSchema (admin/contractor) corrected to internal|client|service; user create/update schemas accept only internal|client
packages/types exports isClientUserType, isMspPrincipalUserType, isInteractiveUserType, isLicensedUserType and INTERACTIVE_USER_TYPES
Portal 'require client' guards (~45 `!== 'client'` sites in client-portal actions/routes, extension proxies) converted to isClientUserType; service users are denied

MSP-data-scope sites converted to isMspPrincipalUserType (clients/projects/tickets list-search predicates, ticket/record visibility, ticketRecordAuthorization, commentActions client guard, documentAuthorization, invoiceQueries, TicketService.ts:396, policyActions.ts:146, userActions assertPortalUserManagementScope, quote sole-approver)
Session/UI sites converted to isInteractiveUserType (getSession, checkTrackedSession, express authMiddleware, middleware.ts portal routing, signin page, Header avatar)
addUser seat check (userActions.ts:557) keyed on isLicensedUserType
Authorization-subject normalizers map 'service' explicitly (authorizationKernel.ts:78, credentialAuthorization.ts:130, workflow crm.ts:969, projects.ts:1078)

Comment author resolution handles service users: comment.ts:99,235, commentActions.ts:536, commentAuthorResolution.ts:61, optimizedTicketActions.ts:3450 never classify a service author as client/contact
Activity actor kind, mention-recipient kind and `|| 'internal'` defaults (latestActivityActor.ts, internalNotificationSubscriber, UserService, userActions, sessionActions) handle 'service' explicitly
User.getAll / getAllUsers / getAllUsersBasic exclude service users unless includeServicePrincipals: true; userTypeFilter={null} pickers exclude them too
UserService list, search and user_type stats exclude service users by default

REST-reachable 'must be internal' checks that mean 'MSP-side caller' accept MSP principals (TicketService.ts:2785, taskCommentService.ts:83,172, ApiTimeSheetController, ApiTicketController, documents routes); human-meaning checks stay internal; classification recorded in SCRATCHPAD
Role assignment (policyActions.ts:453/457, roleActions.ts:106/110) allows a service user to hold MSP roles and rejects client roles
RBAC resolution (three rbac.ts copies, search/acl.ts, tags/permissions.ts, user-composition/permissions.ts, kernel builtinProvider) uses isMspPrincipalUserType explicitly
createServicePrincipal creates the service user (locked sentinel password, name mirrored to first_name), service_principals row and MSP role grants in one transaction after checkServicePrincipalLimit
updateServicePrincipal edits name, description, roles and allow_act_as (allow_act_as requires service_principal:update); name stays mirrored to users.first_name
setServicePrincipalActive(false) sets users.is_inactive, agents.active=false (mcp_agent) and deactivates every active key owned by the principal in one transaction
Reactivating a service principal is limit-checked and does not revive previously deactivated keys

archiveOrDeleteServicePrincipal archives a referenced principal (deactivate, delete keys, set archived_at, clear IdP binding) and hard-deletes only an unreferenced one; mcp_agent_audit is never deleted
issueServicePrincipalKey issues a purpose='service' key owned by the principal (plaintext returned once); revoke and rotate (grace via expireApiKeyAfter) supported
listServicePrincipals returns non-archived principals with kind, roles, act-as flag, status, active key count and last used
No code path other than the service-principal service may insert or update a users row with user_type='service'
createAgent creates a kind='mcp_agent' service principal via createServicePrincipal and is checked against the service-principal limit, not seats
setAgentActive delegates to setServicePrincipalActive
deleteAgent delegates to archiveOrDeleteServicePrincipal; archived agent's (issuer, subject) can be bound to a new agent
resolveAgentByIdp and mintAgentSessionKey use agents.service_user_id; minting refuses an inactive service user
authenticateUser rejects non-interactive user types and requires an explicit userType (untyped User.findUserByEmail fallback removed)
NextAuth signIn callback calls assertInteractiveUser(userId, tenant) for every provider and returns false before recordLoginSuccess, enforceMaxSessions, updateLastLogin or session-row creation
checkTrackedSession, requireLiveSession and sessionAuthMiddleware share INTERACTIVE_USER_TYPES
Mobile handoff, issueMobileOtt, exchangeOttForSession and refreshMobileSession require an active internal user
Apple sign-in via an already-linked apple_user_identities row checks the user is active and internal
IAP restore/provision bind only to an active internal user
ApiKeyService.createApiKey enforces the owner-type × purpose matrix: internal any purpose; service only 'service'; mobile_session and mcp_user internal-only
Password writes refuse service targets: adminChangeUserPassword, UserService password change, PasswordResetService.createResetToken, completePasswordReset, setNewPassword (untyped fallback removed)
ssoPreferences.ts untyped findUserByEmail lookup replaced with a typed internal lookup
Unused duplicate `export const options` / validateUser block in nextAuthOptions.ts removed after confirming no importers
Next middleware and msp/layout redirect a session with a non-interactive user type to sign-in rather than the client portal
assertInternalApiUser replaced by assertMspApiPrincipal (internal | service) at every caller
Both getKeyGateReason copies use an allow-list: active internal or service owners pass, client and unknown types rejected
ApiContext carries principal {userId, userType, kind}, actAsUserId and effectiveUserId; context.userId means effective user; ApiKey type includes agent_id
ServiceContext carries viaPrincipalUserId for model writers

X-Alga-Act-As header validated: principal must be service with allow_act_as (403 ACT_AS_NOT_ALLOWED), target an active internal user in tenant (422 ACT_AS_INVALID_TARGET), human-owned keys rejected (400 ACT_AS_NOT_SUPPORTED)
Under act-as, authorization requires both the principal's and the act-as user's subjects to allow the action (RBAC intersection, record rules evaluated for the human)
assertHumanWorkAssignee(trx, tenant, userIds) guard rejects any non-active-internal id with HUMAN_WORK_ASSIGNEE_INVALID
Ticket assigned_to (create/update), addTicketResourceCore and assignTeamToTicketCore call the human-work guard
ScheduleEntry.create / updateAssignees call the human-work guard
Time-entry owner uses effectiveUserId; a service principal without act-as gets 422 ACT_AS_REQUIRED
Time-sheet owner and approve (approved_by) use effectiveUserId and the human-work guard; service principal without act-as gets ACT_AS_REQUIRED
Time-entry approval requires a human approver (ACT_AS_REQUIRED for a bare service principal)
Project task assigned_to and task_resources call the human-work guard
Interaction owner uses effectiveUserId and the human-work guard
resolveScheduleAssignees never defaults the assignee to a service principal; with no assignees and no act-as the write fails with ACT_AS_REQUIRED
Human-work guard validates only fields the write sets or changes; legacy references to former agent users don't block unrelated edits
Time-entry writers stamp created_via_principal_id / updated_via_principal_id from ServiceContext
Time-sheet approval stamps approved_via_principal_id
Schedule-entry and interaction writers stamp created_via_principal_id
Comment, ticket (entered_via_principal_id) and project-task writers stamp via-principal
ticket_audit_logs records actor_type='service_principal' when a principal acts as itself, and actor_type='user' + via_principal_user_id under act-as
Generic auditLog() records via_principal_user_id in details
MCP call meta-tool accepts act_as_user_id, forwards it as X-Alga-Act-As on the loopback dispatch and records it in mcp_agent_audit.act_as_user_id
Ticket activity feed, time-entry detail and comment header render '<human> via <principal>' and service-authored comments render the principal name with a Service badge/avatar
SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_ENTITLEMENT (Pro only: maxPrincipals, rateLimit ceiling) defined beside TIER_FEATURES; no per-tier map
On Pro the service-principal limit resolves tenants.service_principal_limit → EE appliance claim service_principals → Pro default; CE builds unlimited
checkServicePrincipalLimit(trx, tenant) counts active service users and returns SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_LIMIT_REACHED at the limit
Requests authenticated as a service principal use rate-limit bucket subject sp:<principal user_id> regardless of key (covers MCP per-request keys)
Rate-limit config resolves per-key → per-principal → Pro default; per-principal override capped at the Pro ceiling unless a platform override exists
getServicePrincipalUsage(tenant) returns {limit, used, remaining}
EE AccountManagement page shows a service-principal usage row beside seats with 'don't use seats' note and settings link
Appliance LicenseManagementPage shows the service-principal usage row
Settings → Security → Service principals tab: DataTable (name, kind badge, roles, act-as, status, keys, last used, created by display name) with usage header and New disabled at limit
Create/Edit service principal dialog (name, description, MSP roles, allow act-as switch, optional rate-limit override within ceiling)
Manage keys dialog: issue (shown once), revoke, rotate
EE MCP server settings agent list/create use the service-principal backend and show the shared limit
Settings → Users MSP tab filters with isLicensedUserType; user detail loader rejects service ids
User server actions (adminChangeUserPassword, deleteUser, invite, reactivate) refuse service targets with a pointer to Service principals
API keys admin list shows the owning principal's name with a Service badge instead of username
user_type is immutable to/from 'service' in REST UserService.update and user actions
REST UserService.create rejects user_type='service' and runs checkInternalUserLicenseLimit for internal users

EE migration converts every agent's backing user to user_type='service', sets is_inactive = NOT agents.active, mirrors name, backfills agents.service_user_id and inserts service_principals (kind mcp_agent); idempotent, skips and logs missing/non-internal users
Migration never deactivates or deletes principals to fit the new limit; over-limit tenants only lose the ability to create
OpenAPI documents X-Alga-Act-As and the new error codes on affected routes; MCP and chat API registries regenerated
MCP call tool description documents act_as_user_id and ACT_AS_REQUIRED
New UI strings added to the msp settings locale files
TIER_FEATURES.SERVICE_PRINCIPALS added with FEATURE_MINIMUM_TIER 'pro' (namespace-member pattern like CREDENTIALS)

assertTenantTierAccess(SERVICE_PRINCIPALS) enforced in createServicePrincipal (covers createAgent), reactivation, issueServicePrincipalKey and enabling allow_act_as; below Pro returns 403 TIER_ACCESS_DENIED; no-op on CE
Existing principals on a tenant below Pro (pre-existing or after downgrade) keep authenticating and resolving MCP tokens; only create/reactivate/key issuance is blocked; nothing is deactivated

Below Pro the Service principals tab and MCP agent create flow render TierGate / FeatureUpgradeNotice via useTierFeature; grandfathered principals stay listed with deactivate/delete only; license page row reads 'Available on Pro'
